title: Microsoft Teams: QR code images from external senders are blurred by default
notes: claim 40: severity major on a rationale: risk rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the external access control is described without the documented exception that custom user policies can override the organisation's domain list. The QR code behaviour, default and rollout dates are supported, but the claim that the feature reads no new data is not documented.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: Teams blurs images containing QR codes in messages from external senders.
claims.quote: When an external user sends a message that contains an image with a QR code, Teams blurs the image.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Recipients can select Reveal QR code to reveal the image before viewing or scanning it.
claims.quote: Users must explicitly reveal the image before they can view or scan the QR code. Users can select Reveal QR code to view or scan the QR code.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; title; summary; controls[0].note; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: QR code obscuring is enabled by default.
claims.quote: This experience is enabled by default, and there are no admin controls to enable or disable it.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; controls[0].api; summary; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no admin UI or API control to enable or disable QR code obscuring.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams QR code obscuring admin controls PowerShell configuration licensing meter detection; "Teams" "QR code obscuring" "PowerShell" "allow"; QR code obscuring Graph. Opened QR code obscuring in Microsoft Teams: "there are no admin controls to enable or disable it."

claims.claim: Microsoft describes obscuring as precautionary protection encouraging deliberate interaction with QR codes that can be used in phishing and fraud.
claims.quote: This precautionary protection helps increase user awareness and encourages more deliberate interaction with QR code content, which can be used in phishing and fraud attempts.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A blurred QR code does not mean Teams has identified the code as malicious.
claims.quote: A blurred QR code doesn't mean that Teams identified the QR code as malicious. Teams applies this protection to reduce risk and help users make more informed decisions when interacting with QR codes.

claims.claim: Learn documents support on Teams desktop, web and mobile clients.
claims.quote: This experience is supported on Teams desktop, web, and mobile clients.

claims.claim: For users in China on Teams mobile, QR code obscuring applies to messages from both internal and external users.
claims.quote: For users in China on Teams mobile, this experience applies to QR codes in messages sent by both internal and external users.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: The tenant external access row decides which external organisations users can chat with, without qualifying the effect of custom external access policies.
claims.quote: Custom policy assigned to user: The value for Allow or block external domains setting in the custom policy takes precedence over organization settings.
claims.fix: Change controls[1].governs to 'Organisation-level external domain list for Teams chat'. Replace the first sentence of its note, and narrow the equivalent statements in Risk assessment and Governance controls, to: 'Sets the organisation-level external domain list; users assigned a custom external access policy communicate with domains specified in that policy, not the organisation settings.' Keep the existing sentence that this does not change QR code image display. The qualification is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/trusted-organizations-external-meetings-chat.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: External domain access controls do not change QR code blurring for messages from an allowed external sender.
claims.quote: This experience applies to QR codes in Teams messages sent by external users. This experience is enabled by default, and there are no admin controls to enable or disable it.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature's Learn page lists no licence or prerequisite.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "QR code" "licensing" "obscuring"; Microsoft Teams licensing requirements each user Teams license. Opened QR code obscuring in Microsoft Teams and Manage Teams licenses; the feature page has no licensing or prerequisites section or requirement.

claims.claim: The feature's Learn page names no meter.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams QR code obscuring admin controls PowerShell configuration licensing meter detection; "Teams" "QR code" "licensing" "obscuring". Opened QR code obscuring in Microsoft Teams; no meter, rate or billing unit is stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown and Microsoft has not published licensing for this feature.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included'. Replace the blanket licensing-unknown wording in licensing.notes, Cost and licensing, Open questions and the cost rationale with: 'Each user in the organisation needs a Teams license to use Teams, except for joining meetings anonymously. Microsoft has not published a licensing requirement specific to QR code obscuring at the time of writing (November 2026).' Cite 'Manage Teams licenses' at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access. Do not claim a separately documented price or that no additional licence is required.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licensing requirement specific to QR code obscuring.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "QR code" "licensing" "obscuring"; Microsoft Teams licensing requirements each user Teams license. Opened QR code obscuring in Microsoft Teams and Manage Teams licenses; reviewed Teams Premium licensing search excerpts. No QR-obscuring-specific licence was stated.

claims.claim: No new data access is described for QR code obscuring.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "QR code obscuring" detection data processing tuning. Opened QR code obscuring in Microsoft Teams and read MC1470410; neither describes additional data access or the detection implementation.

claims.claim: The change reads no new data.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "QR code obscuring" detection data processing tuning. Opened QR code obscuring in Microsoft Teams and read MC1470410. They describe blurring and revealing images, but do not state what data the detection mechanism reads.
claims.fix: Replace 'The change adds a protection and reads no new data' in the risk rationale with 'The change adds a protection; Microsoft does not describe new data access'. This preserves the narrower, checked absence already stated in Risk assessment.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The feature's Learn page does not explain how Teams detects QR codes in images or handles undetected codes.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "QR code obscuring" detection data processing tuning. Opened QR code obscuring in Microsoft Teams; it describes the displayed blur and Reveal QR code action, not detection algorithms or missed detections.

claims.claim: No autonomous action beyond the described obscuring experience is documented; the user chooses to reveal the image.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Teams QR code obscuring message images other content types autonomous action admin tune trusted sender domain allowlist Graph. Opened QR code obscuring in Microsoft Teams and read MC1470410; they describe automatic blurring and a user-selected reveal, not other actions.

claims.claim: The feature page describes QR codes in Teams messages and does not describe other content types.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Teams QR code obscuring message images other content types autonomous action admin tune trusted sender domain allowlist Graph. Opened QR code obscuring in Microsoft Teams; its described content is images containing QR codes in Teams messages.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: No tuning or trusted-sender/domain allow-list control for QR code obscuring is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "QR code obscuring" "PowerShell" "allow"; Microsoft Teams QR code obscuring admin tune trusted sender domain allowlist Graph. Opened QR code obscuring in Microsoft Teams and external access reference; no QR-obscuring exception or tuning control was documented.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The known cost is indirect administrative and help desk work, rated low rather than a documented charge or meter.
claims.quote: Review existing user education materials related to phishing awareness, QR code safety, and external collaboration. Update internal help desk documentation to reflect the new user experience.

claims.claim: Impact is medium even though its rationale explicitly describes a change to default behaviour.
claims.quote: Page: 'impact: "medium"'; 'Medium. It changes default behaviour for users who receive images with QR codes from external senders'. Assessment scale: 'high: most users, or a change to default behaviour.'
claims.fix: Set impact to 'high' and replace the impact rationale with: 'High. It changes default behaviour for users who receive images with QR codes from external senders, so those users and the help desk will notice; users with no such messages will not.'
